question: Question: realistic robots have 2-4 arms (humanoid, AMR w/ 4 graspers). Is GR00T 'one core per arm', or does the backbone share? How to benchmark multi-arm?
key_context: GR00T N1.5 is a UNIFIED whole-body policy. The embodiment we already benchmark (Fourier GR1, gr1_arms_only, eid 24) is BIMANUAL -- one policy, one forward pass ALREADY drives TWO arms.

exp1_action_head_dof_decomposition.finding: Adding arms is nearly free. The action head's DoF-dependent parts (action_encoder + action_decoder) are ~1-3% of its latency; the DiT diffusion body (DoF-INVARIANT) dominates. The backbone (ViT+LLM) doesn't know how many arms exist.
exp1_action_head_dof_decomposition.dof_invariant: DiT body (runs x4 denoise = 5.53ms = 92%), vlln (0.386), state_encoder; these are fixed regardless of arm count
exp1_action_head_dof_decomposition.four_arm_projection_DERIVED: 2 arms (action_dim 32) -> 4 arms (action_dim ~64) ~doubles only the 0.054ms encoder/decoder -> +~0.05ms = +0.3% e2e. One brain per ROBOT, not one core per arm.

exp2_camera_view_scaling.finding: Perception (cameras/views) is the real scaling cost -- dwarfs the ~0.05ms DoF cost. More arms usually means more wrist cameras.
exp2_camera_view_scaling.vit_scaling: SUBLINEAR -- batching amortizes: per-view 1.98 -> 0.96 ms (2x efficiency at 4 views)
exp2_camera_view_scaling.llm_scaling: superlinear per doubling (1.48x then 1.71x) -- O(n^2) attention emerging as vision context grows
exp2_camera_view_scaling.takeaway: each camera ~ +1ms ViT (amortizes well) + a growing LLM-context tax; the ViT+LLM path (2-5ms each) is 40-100x the DoF cost

exp3_independent_agents_case_B.when: If the N arms are INDEPENDENT agents (separate brains / independently tasked graspers), not a unified policy -> N x full backbone -> THROUGHPUT regime -> literally one core per arm.

bottom_line: For a unified robot (humanoid / coordinated AMR) GR00T cost is set by SENSING + THINKING (shared ViT+LLM), not by the number of ARMS (acting is ~free). It's one big core per ROBOT. 'One core per arm' applies only to INDEPENDENT agents, where it becomes a throughput problem.
_correction_2026-10-12_per_step_weightin: DEFECT in dof_dependent_fraction.four_step_weighted_DiT_x4 and four_arm_projection_DERIVED: GR00T's flow-matching loop runs action_encoder -> DiT -> action_decoder on EVERY denoise step, so the DoF-dependent graphs must be weighted x4 like the DiT. Corrected (DERIVED, 5090): DoF-dependent = 4 x 0.054 = 0.216 ms per inference = 3.5% of the action head (0.216 / 6.145 ms), not 0.90%; 2->4-arm projection ~doubles it -> +~0.22 ms = ~1.3% of the 17.2 ms MEASURED e2e, not +0.3%. Component ms values are per single call. Conclusion (arms nearly free) unchanged.
